profile.summary: Mumbai-based drug maker founded by Dr Habil Khorakiwala. Three pillars: (1) a generic and branded pharmaceuticals business (~77% of FY26 revenue per ICRA) in the UK (CP Pharmaceuticals, Wrexham: hospital injectables, pharmacy, OTC, export; 18% share of its covered market), Ireland (Pinewood: liquids and creams), India (diabetes, orthopaedics, pain, regenerative derma, and the Emrok/Miqnaf antibiotics) and emerging markets; (2) insulin biosimilars (human insulin and glargine, ~21% of FY26 revenue, sold in 30+ emerging markets and India); (3) novel antibiotics: six USFDA QIDP-designated molecules, of which Zaynich (cefepime/zidebactam, WCK 5222) was approved by the USFDA and CDSCO in May 2026. 11-12 manufacturing sites (India, UK, Ireland), two R&D centres, ~3,200 employees; 78% of revenue from outside India. Exited US generics (Chapter 7 liquidation of the US subsidiaries, 11-Jul-2025).

shares.note: Unchanged at Jun-2026 (no allotment except 6,600 ESOP shares in Aug-2025). Enabling resolution for up to ₹3,000 cr of equity/convertibles approved for the AGM of 10-Aug-2026 (not used by 30-Sep-2026: promoter stake 49.09% at Jun-2026).

exceptionals.item: Deconsolidation of US subsidiaries (Chapter 7, 11-Jul-2025) and trustee settlement
Final settlement with Dr Reddy's of the ₹300 cr holdback under the 2020 business transfer

fy26.taxNote: Tax losses utilised with no deferred tax asset created: ₹118 cr of tax in FY26; domestic rate 34.944% (old regime; MAT credit ₹196 cr on the balance sheet); unabsorbed-loss DTA ₹277 cr.

q1fy27.note: No earnings call was held for Q1FY27 (we found none on BSE/Screener); the last management Q&A before 30-Sep was the investor meet of 4-Jun-2026.

guidance.said: Slow increase at first; 'wait for 12-18 months and then you would see a very different trajectory' (hockey stick).
Slight loss or neutral for the first 12-18 months (the MD clarified: Zaynich only, not the company); breakeven in 12, at most 18, months.
Globally US$1.5-2bn a year at peak (no year given); the US is normally ~40% of global revenue; long-term share 20-25% of resistant cases.
US: new antibiotics cost US$1,200-1,500 a day, US$10,000-15,000 a course; Wockhardt will be price-neutral to them. India: 75-80% discount to US.
Director Zahabiya Khorakiwala: new anti-infectives in the US typically do ~US$30-50mn collectively over their first ~three years.
Normal capex ₹200-300 cr a year for three years, mainly biologics capacity; R&D at about the same percentage of sales.
Biosimilars to double in 24-36 months; capacity doubles in 12-15 months; five pipeline insulins (aspart, aspart 30/70, degludec, degludec+aspart, semaglutide) launch after ~two years.
EMA approval of Zaynich expected by the end of calendar 2026; EU file under accelerated assessment.
Launch Zaynich in 7-8 high-resistance markets (LatAm, Eurasia, GCC, South/South-East Asia) in 18-24 months; no partners: build own organisation.
ICRA expects CFO of ₹400-420 cr in FY27, capex ~₹300 cr in each of FY27-28, external debt repayments ₹171 cr (FY27) and ₹198 cr (FY28); promoter loans likely to be reduced (discretionary).
US entry end-2026 or early 2027 (product available ~Q1 CY2027); India launch around Dec-2026/Jan-2027 through the anti-infectives field force (Business Today).
₹6,000 cr revenue by FY28 and ₹12,000 cr by FY31 (Business Today; not in company filings).

specified fixed assets + pledge of promoter shares
current assets, factory land and buildings
movable fixed assets + pledge of shares (₹75 cr prepaid in FY26)
Pinewood assets; EUR 16.6mn bullet in Jul-2028

fundRaises.what: Sale of part of the India branded business (62 brands, Baddi plant) to Dr Reddy's
fundRaises.note: ₹300 cr held back against revenue benchmarks; settled for ₹35.35 cr effective 31-Mar-2026. FY21 gain of ₹1,470 cr (pre-tax) shown in discontinued operations.
Net ₹977.8 cr: ₹500 cr debt repayment, ₹227.8 cr general purposes, ₹250 cr capex/R&D (₹162.3 cr unused at Mar-26, redeployed to all R&D incl. NCEs, to FY28).
Not used by 30-Sep-2026. Earlier enablers: ₹1,600 cr (2023), ₹1,000 cr (2024), ₹2,000 cr (2025, unused).

pipeline.what: Cefepime + zidebactam (a beta-lactam 'enhancer'), IV, hospital; active against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas
pipeline.usStatus: USFDA approved 30-May-2026 (NDA 220787, holder Wockhardt Bio AG; filed 30-Sep-2025, priority review, QIDP, fast track) for complicated urinary tract infections incl. pyelonephritis in adults. QIDP adds 5 years of exclusivity. US supply from a USFDA-approved contract manufacturer in Europe; commercial operations through an operating partner (3PL, pharmacovigilance) with Wockhardt's own leadership team.
pipeline.indiaStatus: CDSCO import and marketing authorisation 27-May-2026 (cUTI incl. pyelonephritis, with concurrent Gram-negative bacteraemia), after the Subject Expert Committee's favourable recommendation of 10-Mar-2026. The Q1FY27 release (10-Aug-2026) still carries the earlier line 'full approval after CMC data review expected by Q3FY27', which we read as the locally manufactured product (not confirmed).
pipeline.euStatus: MAA filed with the EMA; accelerated assessment granted; EMA confirmed the dossier adequate for review for cUTI, cIAI, HAP/VAP and BSI (Q1FY27 release). Management expected approval by the end of calendar 2026. No CHMP opinion by 30-Sep-2026.
pipeline.launch: India ~Dec-2026/Jan-2027; US end-2026/early-2027 (available ~Q1 CY2027); EM 7-8 markets within 18-24 months of Jun-2026; EU after approval.
pipeline.patent: Composition patent to 2038 (more filings to extend); QIDP gives at least 10 years of exclusivity from approval in the US.
pipeline.capitalised: ₹1,055 cr carried as intangible asset under development at Mar-26 (₹848 cr at Mar-25); to be capitalised by FY28 and then amortised.
pipeline.phase3: ENHANCE-1 vs meropenem in cUTI (530 patients): composite cure 89% vs 68.4% at test-of-cure (Business Today); management cites 96.8% composite at end of therapy and ~20 points superiority; 85+ compassionate-use patients.

pipeline.what: Oral ketolide (macrolide class) for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia; 3-day course
pipeline.indiaStatus: Approved and launched in India (launch May-2025, ICRA); DCGI removed the 'supply condition' in FY26, widening access; field force expanded. India only (no plans abroad).
pipeline.capitalised: ₹201 cr intangible under development at Mar-26 (to be capitalised by FY30).

pipeline.indiaStatus: Launched in India in Jun-2020. FY26 growth ~50-60% (Emrok/Emrok O +106% in Q4FY26, +60% FY26; +29% in Q1FY27); approved in Uganda; Russian licensing partner. NCEs (mostly Emrok) were ~2% of FY26 revenue (ICRA split 77% formulations / 21% biosimilars / balance NCEs).

pipeline.what: IV first-line therapy for ESBL infections
pipeline.indiaStatus: India phase 3 (324 cUTI/AP patients) completed, matched meropenem; India NDA filing planned in Q3FY27.
pipeline.capitalised: ₹350 cr intangible under development at Mar-26 (to be capitalised by FY30).

pipeline.status: Phase 1 completed in the US; the dose change means a phase 2 trial is likely needed; chairman: no product comes in less than four years.

pipeline.what: Biosimilars for India and emerging markets
pipeline.status: Aspart R in phase 3; others in R&D/PK-PD; launches 'after two years'.

successRates.note: BIO / Informa Pharma Intelligence / QLS Advisors, Clinical Development Success Rates 2011-2020 (all indications).

intangiblesUnderDevelopment.note: Key audit matter (recoverability). Screener shows these inside CWIP (₹2,379 cr at Mar-26 = tangible CWIP ~₹671 cr + ₹1,708 cr).

accounting.rdCapitalisation: Total R&D was ~10% of revenue in FY26 (AR MD&A) but only ₹120 cr (3.6%) was expensed; the rest (~₹215 cr) was capitalised as NCE development. Reported EBITDA therefore excludes most R&D; it returns later as amortisation.
accounting.otherIncomeNote: FY26 other income ₹111 cr = interest ₹7 cr + other non-operating ₹104 cr (liabilities written back ₹15 cr, profit on sale of assets ₹55 cr, rest ₹34 cr). FY25 ₹62 cr (written back ₹23 cr, asset sales ₹3 cr).
accounting.auditor: MSKC & Associates LLP (appointed AGM 28-Jun-2024 for five years); unmodified opinion on FY26.
accounting.secretarialAudit: Receivables, guarantee fees and payables with Wockhardt Bio AG overdue beyond RBI/FEMA timelines (₹207 cr overdue receivables at Mar-26).

minorities.holdsWhat: UK (CP Pharmaceuticals, Wockhardt UK), Ireland (Pinewood), continental Europe, Wockhardt Suisse USA LLC (Zaynich US), the Zaynich US NDA, and IP/marketing authorisations.
minorities.openQuestion: The AR does not name the 14.15% holders. The related-party annexure lists the promoter directors' 'direct or indirect' shareholding in Bio AG as 95.47%; we could not confirm who holds the minority.

history.event: Wockhardt Ltd incorporated (CIN L24230MH1999PLC120720) as the listed vehicle of Dr Habil Khorakiwala's pharma business; antibiotic discovery programme running since the 1990s (~US$800mn invested over 25 years per the chairman).
history.impact: Long R&D bet funded through repeated crises.

history.event: USFDA import alert on the Waluj plant (Aurangabad); UK MHRA action followed. Nov-2013: import alert on Chikalthana (Aurangabad).
history.impact: US generics business crippled; both alerts are still on the FDA's import alert 66-40 list.

history.event: Import alert on the Ankleshwar API plant; warning letters followed (Ankleshwar 2016-17; Morton Grove, Illinois, 2017; consent decree with the US DoJ; Morton Grove plant disposed by Jun-2024).
history.impact: Third Indian site barred from the US.

history.event: Sold 62 India brands and the Baddi plant to Dr Reddy's for ₹1,850 cr (₹300 cr holdback).
history.impact: FY21 profit ₹686 cr is almost all this gain: continuing operations lost ₹297 cr; discontinued operations made ₹985 cr after ₹499 cr of tax (gain ₹1,470 cr pre-tax). India business shrank to ~₹500-700 cr.

history.event: UK government reserved a fill-finish line at CP Pharmaceuticals, Wrexham, for COVID-19 vaccines (AstraZeneca); 2022: 15-year fill-finish collaboration with a global vaccine company (Serum) for up to 150mn doses a year, profit share 51:49 in Bio AG's favour.
history.impact: UK vaccines revenue; Wrexham injectables capacity.

history.event: Equity raised to survive: rights issue ₹748 cr (FY22), QIP ₹468 cr (Mar-2024), QIP ₹1,000 cr (Nov-2024 at ₹1,105). Promoter stake fell from 74% (2017) to 49.1%.
history.impact: Share count up from 11.1 cr to 16.2 cr; debt down; liquidity crisis of 2018-23 ended.
Second in-house NCE franchise in India.

history.event: US subsidiaries Morton Grove Pharmaceuticals and Wockhardt USA filed for Chapter 7 liquidation; deconsolidated.
history.impact: Exit from loss-making US generics (FY25 US revenue US$11mn); ₹110 cr exceptional charge in FY26.

history.event: Zaynich NDA submitted to the USFDA (accepted Dec-2025, priority review); first quarterly profit of the new regime (Jul-Sep 2025 PBT ₹91 cr).
history.impact: Our turnaround window starts the next day (1-Oct-2025).

history.event: Final settlement with Dr Reddy's of the 2020 holdback (₹35 cr gain).
history.impact: Closes the last dispute of the 2020 sale.

history.event: CDSCO approval of Zaynich; 30-May-2026 USFDA approval (first India-discovered NCE approved by the FDA).
history.impact: Stock +19% on 1-Jun-2026 to a record; launch costs begin.

history.event: ICRA upgraded long-term rating to [ICRA]A- (Stable) from BBB (Positive).
history.impact: Cheaper debt; confirms the balance-sheet repair.

management.name: Dr Habil Khorakiwala
management.note: Re-appointed Jun-2024; AGM 2026 resolution lifts his pay ceiling to ₹10 cr a year from Mar-2027 (up to ₹15 cr later); pay ratio 79.3x the median employee in FY26.

management.name: Dr Murtaza Khorakiwala
management.note: Runs operations; led the cost and portfolio clean-up (EBITDA margin 5.4% to 18.6% in three years).

management.name: Zahabiya Khorakiwala
management.role: Non-executive director; leads the US Zaynich launch; Executive Co-chairperson of Wockhardt Bio AG from 4-May-2026 (US$250,000 a year)
management.note: Previously MD of Wockhardt Hospitals for 15 years; no prior US pharma commercial experience.

management.name: Bill McNey (CCO, US novel antibiotics), Dr Dennis Deruelle (CMO, US), Leo Yasinski (VP market access), Sandy Estrada (field medical)
management.note: McNey helped launch Shionogi's Fetroja (cefiderocol), Zaynich's main rival; Yasinski launched Zerbaxa and others at Cubist/Merck.

management.name: Annapurna Das
management.role: President, India business and NCE emerging markets

management.name: Dr Mahesh Patel / Dr Sachin Bhagwat
management.role: Chief Scientific Mentor / Chief Scientific Officer
management.note: Led the antibiotic discovery programme for 25+ years.

governance.board: Nine directors at Mar-26: four from the promoter family (chairman, MD, executive director, non-executive Zahabiya) and five independent (V K Jairath, Akhilesh Gupta, Amelia Fernandes, Amb. Ahmad Javed, O P Bhatt from Nov-2025).

promoterHolding.note: Pledged shares secure the company's own NBFC term loans (Tata Capital, Axis Finance, STCI). Jun-2026 pledge figure not found; latest disclosed is Mar-2026.

governance.promoterLoans: ~₹950 cr lent to the company by promoter entities at 5.92-12.3% (₹748 cr non-current), repayable by 20-Jun-2027 with an option to renew.
governance.plants: Three Indian sites (Waluj, Chikalthana, Ankleshwar API) remain on USFDA import alert 66-40 (since 2013 and 2016). ICRA (May-2026): 'no major open regulatory issues currently' because the US business was exited; Zaynich for the US is made by a USFDA-approved contract manufacturer in Europe. UK (Wrexham) and Ireland sites supply their home markets.
governance.relatedParty: Material RPT approvals sought with Wockhardt Bio AG (85.85% owned) of up to ₹1,000 cr a year incl. IP transfers at independent valuation (FY26: Wockhardt Ltd bought ₹278 cr of IP from Bio AG); overdue FEMA receivables from Bio AG flagged by the secretarial auditor.
